answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake in a shared bridge escrow before it may trade: the stake acts like a ferrous anchor — heavy, hard to duplicate cheaply, and forfeited if the agent cheats. New identities start with an opal-tier trust cap, earning higher limits only through verified, settled trades over time. Spinning up thousands of fake agents then costs real capital per identity, while honest agents recover their bond and graduate to full trust.
